desc:
The string expr is a boolean expression without spaces. It uses the constants t (true) and f (false), the unary operator ! (not), the binary operators & (and), ^ (exclusive or) and | (or), and round brackets.

Priorities from highest to lowest: !, then &, then ^, then |. Binary operators of equal priority are applied from left to right. ! applies to the single operand right after it, which may be a constant, a bracketed expression or another ! (!!t is true). Brackets override priorities.

Return the value of the expression.

Examples: t|f&f is t | (f & f), so true. !(t|t) is false. t^t^t is (t ^ t) ^ t, so true.
constraints: expr contains only the characters t, f, !, &, ^, |, ( and ) and is a valid expression
Brackets are balanced and can be nested deeply (up to 3,000 levels)
hints: It is the same problem as evaluating an arithmetic expression with priorities, just with booleans. Use two stacks: one for values and one for operators.
Give each operator a priority (|=1, ^=2, &=3, !=4). Before pushing a binary operator, apply the stacked operators with priority greater than or equal to it.

! is a prefix operator: push it without popping anything, and apply it later (when a binary operator with lower priority arrives, when a bracket closes, or at the end). Closing a bracket applies operators down to the matching (; a ! in front of the bracket stays on the stack and is applied afterwards.
editorial: Use the shunting-yard method with a value stack and an operator stack. t and f push True or False. ( and ! are pushed directly: a prefix operator has no left operand, so it cannot trigger any application of operators on the stack.

For a binary operator c pop and apply the operators on top while the top is not ( and has a priority at least that of c; then push c. Applying a binary operator pops two values, applying ! pops one. A ) applies operators until it reaches the matching (. At the end apply whatever is left; the value stack then holds the answer.

A ! that is directly in front of a bracket sits below the ( on the operator stack, so it is applied after the bracket's content has been reduced to one value, which is exactly right. Time and space are O(n).
